blocks.heading: Levels of specialisation
blocks.text: Specialisation can be considered between countries, between regions, between industries and between individual businesses. At each level a unit concentrates on activities suited to its resources or capabilities. A level describes the scale of concentration; it is not a rank in a management hierarchy. Different levels can exist at the same time.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A coastal region concentrates on fishing, while a particular business concentrates on repairing fishing equipment. The region’s concentration is regional specialisation. The repair firm’s focus is specialisation between businesses. The examples do not identify a managing director or supervisor: those are management levels, not levels of specialisation. Concentration creates reasons to exchange with other regions or businesses for goods and services not produced locally.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why a coastal region concentrating on fishing illustrates a different classification from a supervisor managing a team.

The region illustrates a level of specialisation: concentration of activity across an area. A supervisor’s position belongs to management hierarchy. The test is whether the classification describes a focus of economic activity or a rank of authority; neither can be substituted for the other.
